summary: Arnold J. Toynbee worked in history and archaeology. Educated at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford, he held posts at King's College London (circa 1919-1924), Chatham House (circa 1925-1955), and the London School of Economics (circa 1925-1955).

Arnold Kunst worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and University of Warsaw under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, Stanisław Schayer, and Erich Frauwallner. He taught at Lviv, SOAS, and Cambridge.

Arsène Darmesteter was a linguist who studied at INALCO, the École des chartes, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Gaston Paris. He held posts at EPHE, the Séminaire Israélite de France, the University of Paris, and ENS.

Artemij Keidan is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (2001-2005), where he became an Associate Professor in 2020, and was a Russian language lecturer at the University of L'Aquila (2009-2010).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig under Theodor Benfey, Friedrich Max Müller, and Rudolf von Roth. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1880-1899) and held fellowships at Balliol.

Arthur Berriedale Keith worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Julius Eggeling and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office and lectured at the University of Edinburgh (1914-1944).

Arthur Christensen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at the University of Copenhagen under Michael Viggo Fausbøll, Johannes Edvard Lehmann, and Friedrich Carl Andreas, he served as a Docent at the University of Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.

Arthur Coke Burnell worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke, and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1860.
Arthur Evans was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He received his education at Harrow School (circa 1865-1870) and Brasenose College (1870).
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank, later serving on the faculty at Stanford (1947, professor 1958) and Yale (1959, 1961).

Arthur Galletti was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his education at Cheltenham College and Trinity College, Oxford, before serving as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1900 to 1934.

Arthur Haberlandt worked in the field of history and archaeology, among other disciplines. Succeeding Michael Haberlandt in 1924, he held an academic post at the University of Vienna from circa 1914 to 1945.

Arthur Henry Ewing worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Washington & Jefferson College, Pittsburgh Theological Seminary, and Johns Hopkins. He led Christian Boys' Boarding School and Ewing Christian College, and was a fellow at the University of Allahabad.

Arthur Henry Fox Strangways worked in Indology. He studied classics at Balliol College, Oxford (circa 1878-1882) and attended the Berlin University of the Arts, later serving as a schoolmaster at Dulwich College (1884-1886) and Wellington College (1886-1910).
Arthur James Beattie was a scholar in the field of linguistics. He was educated at Montrose Academy, the University of Aberdeen (circa 1931-1935), and the University of Cambridge (circa 1935-1938).

Arthur Leslie Saunders was active in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (circa 1880-1882), joined the Indian Civil Service in 1880, and later held a post at the India Office (1918-1923).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian. He studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett, later becoming Professor of the History of South Asia there. He also headed the Department of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (1965-1979).
Arthur Marshman Spencer was a scholar in the field of Indology. He completed his education at Kingswood School and Headingley College.

Arthur Mason Tippetts Jackson worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his M.A. at the University of Oxford (circa 1884-1888) and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1888 to 1909.
